summary:
The "Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act" or "KIDS Act" (H.R. 7757, 119th Cong.) is an omnibus bill establishing federal requirements for online platforms, chatbots, and gaming services concerning minors (defined in § 2(8) as individuals under 17), enforced primarily by the FTC. It contains six titles.

**Title I ("SCREEN Act")** requires providers of "covered platforms"—platforms where more than one-third of material is "sexual material harmful to minors" knowingly made available—to adopt commercially available "technology verification measures" and prevent minor access, beginning one year post-enactment (§ 103). Providers may not require government-issued ID (§ 103(e)), must observe data-minimization and security standards, and the FTC must consult specified experts (§ 104). GAO must report within three years (§ 105). Section 106 preempts state laws imposing parallel verification mandates, subject to savings clauses for tort, contract, criminal, and consumer-protection laws.

**Title II** defines "covered platform" (§ 201) and contains four subtitles. **Subtitle A ("Kids Online Safety Act")** requires reasonable policies addressing enumerated harms without imposing a duty of care (§ 213(c)(2)), minor safeguards and parental tools with most-protective default settings (§ 214), reporting mechanisms with a 10-day response window (§ 215), disclosures and verifiable parental consent (§ 216), advertising labels (§ 217), a prohibition on advertising illegal products to minors (§ 218), and annual independent third-party audits with FTC and public reporting (§ 219). Section 220 disclaims any age-verification mandate; § 221 preempts conflicting state law. **Subtitle B ("SMK Act")** prohibits ephemeral messaging for minors (§ 233) and direct messaging for children under 13 (§ 234), and mandates parental direct-messaging controls for teens (§ 235), with an encryption savings clause (§ 236); effective 180 days post-enactment except § 235 (§ 238). **Subtitle C ("SPY Kids Act")** prohibits market/product research on minors subject to exceptions (§ 243); effective 90 days post-enactment (§ 245).

**Title III ("Safer GAMING Act")** requires online video game providers to supply default-enabled, most-protective communication safeguards and parental tools (§ 303).

**Title IV ("SAFE BOTs Act")** prohibits chatbots from falsely claiming professional licensure (§ 403), mandates AI-status and crisis-resource disclosures (§ 404), and requires break advisories after three hours and harm-mitigation policies (§ 405).

**Title V** mandates multiple studies and reports (FTC, HHS, NIH), and amends Subtitle A of the Protecting Children in the 21st Century Act (15 U.S.C. 6551 et seq.) by striking and replacing §§ 211–214, 216 to establish an FTC public-awareness campaign with ten years of annual reports (§ 522). It creates a Commerce-administered Kids Internet Safety Partnership that sunsets five years after establishment (§ 526).

**Title VI** provides FTC enforcement via FTC Act § 18(a)(1)(B) and state parens patriae actions (§ 601), vests exclusive constitutional-challenge jurisdiction in the D.C. Circuit with 90/60-day limitations (§ 602), includes First Amendment, Section 230, encryption, and COPPA savings clauses (§ 603), severability (§ 604), and a general one-year effective date (§ 605). The bill authorizes no appropriations.
